title: Gothic Horror
description: The first decades of film history brought many attempts to adapt Gothic novels for the screen, and works such as Frankenstein and Dracula still shape the popular imagination today.

title: Gangster Films
description: The early 1930s, the so-called "golden age of turbulence", was a period when censorship was suspended. Mae West was at her peak, wildly surreal musicals were being made and armed gangsters were lurking.

title: Color in Film
description: In the early days of cinema, films were dominated by black and white. It was a long road from frame-by-frame hand painting to the refinement seen in The Wizard of Oz.

title: The First Animated Films
description: In 1908, Fantasmagorie, by Émile Cohl (1857-1938), fascinated audiences by showing what animation could do. Twenty-nine years later, the first animated feature film was released, opening the doors of imagination on the big screen.

title: Society on Screen
description: During the economic turmoil of the Great Depression, movies offered an affordable window onto the world for the price of a ticket.

title: Hollywood in the Shadow of War
description: Even before the United States entered the war, Hollywood had been turning out a series of films with propagandistic leanings and, weeks before Pearl Harbor, was already making patriotic war movies.

title: Depression-Era Musicals
description: Musicals dominated movie theaters in cinema's early decades, and in the 1930s they captured the recklessness and feverish energy people showed in the face of the Great Depression.

title: Sound and Comedy
description: When talkies replaced silent films in the late 1920s, comedians took radical steps to adapt to the new possibilities, and new masters of comedy took the spotlight.

title: The Romantic Comedy of the 1930s
description: It makes perfect sense that the name of the most American of all film genres comes from baseball. The screwball comedy, a kind of grandfather of the romantic comedy, is made up of fast-paced, irreverent pictures, and it peaked in the 1930s and 1940s.
